tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

18	**断点续跑（resumable）。** 百万级 PDF 的批处理不可能一次跑完：机器会崩、任务会被抢占、你会主动中断。olmOCR 的做法是把队列的**持久状态**全部落在 workspace 的文件里（u1-l3 介绍过五大产物），内存里的 `asyncio.Queue` 只是每次启动时从磁盘重建出来的临时视图。本讲会精确回答「哪些东西落盘、哪些东西在内存」。

20	**乐观并发与「标记」语义。** 多台机器（或多个进程）可能同时指向同一个 workspace。olmOCR 不用中心化的锁服务，而是用两个约定俗成的「标记」协调：
21	
22	- **done flag**：`done_flags/done_{hash}.flag`，表示某个工作项已完成，任何人都不必再做。
23	- **worker lock**：`worker_locks/worker_{hash}.lock`，表示某个工作项正被某个 worker 处理，别人先别碰。
24

159	### 4.2 populate_queue：去重、分组与 sha1 组哈希
160	
161	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
162	
163	`populate_queue(work_paths, items_per_group)` 解决的问题是：**把一批新文档路径幂等地并入队列索引**。三个关键词：
164	
165	- **幂等**：同一批路径重复传入不会产生重复分组。pipeline 里 `main()` 每次带 `--pdfs` 启动都会调用它，重跑是常态。
166	- **分组**：新路径按 `items_per_group` 个一组切分。u2-l2 讲过这个数由「目标页数 ÷ 平均页数」估出；tarball 则固定每组 1 个（见 pipeline.py 的两次调用）。
167	- **组哈希**：每组算一个 sha1 作为身份。这个哈希是后续一切协调的钥匙——done flag、worker lock、结果文件名都用它。
168	
169	为什么哈希前要先 `sorted`？因为 Python 的 set 迭代顺序受字符串哈希随机化影响（PYTHONHASHSEED），同一组路径在不同进程里的顺序可能不同。先排序再哈希，保证**任何机器、任何时刻**对同一路径集合算出同一个 ID。公式化地说，对路径集合 \( G \)：
170	
171	\[ \mathrm{hash}(G) = \mathrm{sha1}\big(\,\texttt{utf8}(p_1) \,\Vert\, \texttt{utf8}(p_2) \,\Vert\, \cdots \,\Vert\, \texttt{utf8}(p_k)\,\big), \quad p_1 < p_2 < \cdots < p_k = \mathrm{sorted}(G) \]
172	
173	其中 \( \Vert \) 表示字节串直接拼接（无分隔符）。
174	
175	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
176	
177	`populate_queue` 的执行步骤（伪代码）：
178	
179	```text
180	输入: work_paths（新一批路径）, items_per_group
181	1. all_paths  = set(work_paths)                # 入参级去重
182	2. lines      = backend.load_index_lines()      # 读现有索引
183	3. existing   = 解析 lines → {组哈希: [路径...]}
184	4. existing_paths = existing 中所有路径摊平成集合
185	5. new_paths  = sorted(all_paths - existing_paths)   # 跨批次去重 + 排序
186	6. 若 new_paths 为空 → 直接返回（什么都不写）
187	7. 把 new_paths 按 items_per_group 逐段切片
188	   每段算 _compute_workgroup_hash(段) → 得到 (组哈希, 段)
189	8. combined = existing ∪ 新组                  # 同哈希时新组覆盖旧组
190	9. backend.save_index_lines(编码后的 combined)  # 整文件覆盖写
191	```
192	
193	两个值得咀嚼的细节：
194	
195	- **去重是路径级的，不是组级的**。第 5 步在「路径」粒度上做差集。后果：如果第二次运行换了 `items_per_group`，**已有分组不会被重新切分**——旧路径全部命中 `existing_paths` 被剔除，只有新增路径按新的组大小分组。索引一旦写入，分组就冻结了。
196	- **第 5 步的 `sorted` 有双重作用**：既让分组结果确定（同批路径在任何机器上切出相同的组），也让组内顺序确定，进一步稳定组哈希。
197	
198	CSV 编解码是索引的「物理格式」层：每行 `[组哈希, 路径1, 路径2, ...]` 用 `csv.writer` 的 `QUOTE_MINIMAL` 规则转义——只有含逗号/引号的字段才会被双引号包裹，其余裸写。

295	### 4.3 initialize_queue 与 get_work：洗牌、三级跳过与锁
296	
297	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
298	
299	消费侧要回答三个问题：
300	
301	**一、启动时队列从哪来？** `initialize_queue` 把索引重建为内存队列：剔除已有 done flag 的组，剩余的 `random.shuffle` 打乱后灌进 `asyncio.Queue`。为什么要洗牌？两个理由：(1) **负载均衡**——索引按路径排序切组，相邻路径往往同源同长短，不洗牌的话耗时大户可能聚堆，多个 worker 快慢悬殊；(2) **多机错峰**——若两台机器都从头按序消费，会在同样的项目上反复撞锁；随机起点让它们自然散开。
302	
303	**二、领任务时要检查什么？** 内存队列是启动时刻的快照，别的 worker/机器此后可能已经完成了其中某些项。所以 `get_work` 每弹出一项要做**三级跳过检查**：
304	
305	1. 本地 `_completed_hash_cache` 命中 → 跳过（纯内存，零后端 IO）；
306	2. 后端 `is_completed(hash)` → 跳过（一次后端查询）；
307	3. 后端 `is_worker_lock_taken(hash)` 锁被占且未过期 → 跳过（别人正在做）。
308	
309	三级全过 → `create_worker_lock` 抢锁，把这项返回给 worker。
310	
311	**三、锁为什么会「过期」？** worker 崩溃时不会有人来放锁，锁文件会永久残留。olmOCR 的解法是**锁自带新鲜度**：锁是否有效看它的 mtime 距今是否超过 `worker_lock_timeout_secs`（默认 1800 秒）：
312	
313	\[ \text{锁有效} \iff now - \mathrm{mtime}(\text{lock}) \leq 1800\,\text{s} \]
314	
315	超过 30 分钟的锁视为 stale（主人大概率已死），`create_worker_lock` 直接覆盖它（见 [L210](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L210) 的注释 "Create lock (overwrites if stale)"）。这要求工作项的处理时长明显小于 30 分钟——分组大小（约 500 页）正是按这个量级校准的。
316	
317	**best-effort 语义**：锁与旗的写操作失败时只 `logger.warning` 然后继续，不抛异常（LocalBackend 中尤为明确，见 [L339-L351](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L339-L351) 的注释 "duplicate work is okay"）。因为最坏结果只是重复计算，而结果落盘是覆盖写、幂等（u2-l8）；反之，为了严格锁语义而让流水线卡死才是不可接受的。
318	
319	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
320	
321	`initialize_queue`：
322	
323	```text
324	1. lines = backend.load_index_lines()
325	2. work_queue = 解析 lines → {组哈希: [路径...]}
326	3. done_hashes = backend.get_completed_hashes()      # 全量已完成集合
327	4. remaining = work_queue 的键 - done_hashes
328	5. remaining_items = [WorkItem(hash=h, work_paths=...) for h in remaining]
329	6. random.shuffle(remaining_items)                    # 洗牌
330	7. 重建空 self._queue，逐项 put 进去
331	8. 返回 self.size
332	```
333	
334	`get_work` 的主循环：
335	
336	```text
337	while True:
338	    item = self._queue.get_nowait()          # 队列空 → 返回 None（worker 退出）
339	    ① item.hash ∈ 本地已完成缓存 → task_done, continue
340	    ② backend.is_completed(item.hash)  为真 → task_done, continue
341	       连续 ② 命中满 3 次 → 全量刷新本地缓存（此后走①）
342	    ③ backend.is_worker_lock_taken(item.hash) 为真 → task_done, continue
343	    ④ backend.create_worker_lock(item.hash)  # 失败仅告警并 continue
344	    重置连续命中计数，返回 item
345	```
346	
347	`mark_done`：
348	
349	```text
350	1. backend.create_done_flag(item.hash)     # 先立旗
351	2. backend.delete_worker_lock(item.hash)   # 后放锁
352	3. self._queue.task_done()                 # 销账
353	```
354	
355	顺序很关键：**先立旗再放锁**。若反过来（先放锁后立旗），存在一个窗口——锁已删、旗未写——另一个 worker 恰好在此窗口检查会同时通过 ②③，把同一项重复领走。旗先落地，放锁瞬间该 item 已在完成集合里，任何并发检查都会被 ② 拦下。

372	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
373	
374	**实践目标**：在 4.2 的 workspace 上继续——初始化队列、领一个任务、观察锁文件出现、`mark_done` 后观察旗立锁消，最后**重新初始化**验证断点续跑。

376	**操作步骤**：
377	
378	1. 把下面脚本存为 `practice_consume.py`，把 `WS` 改成 4.2 实践打印出的 workspace 路径（或把两段脚本合并成一次运行）：

380	```python
381	# 示例代码：本讲实践脚本（续）
382	import asyncio, os
383	from olmocr.work_queue import LocalBackend, WorkQueue
384	
385	WS = "/tmp/wq_practice_xxxxx"   # ← 换成 4.2 实践的 workspace 路径
386	
387	async def main():
388	    wq = WorkQueue(LocalBackend(WS))          # 同一 workspace，可视为"重启后的新进程"
389	
390	    n = await wq.initialize_queue()
391	    print("初始化后的队列长度:", n)             # 预期 3
392	
393	    item = await wq.get_work()
394	    print("领到工作项:", item.hash[:12], "包含", len(item.work_paths), "个路径")
395	
396	    locks = os.listdir(os.path.join(WS, "worker_locks"))
397	    print("领到后 worker_locks:", locks)       # 预期出现 1 个 worker_{hash}.lock

400	
401	    print("完成后 done_flags:", os.listdir(os.path.join(WS, "done_flags")))  # 1 个 done_{hash}.flag

412	2. 运行脚本，对照输出逐行核对。
413	3. 进阶一步：手动在 `worker_locks/` 下仿造一个别人的新鲜锁——复制现有锁文件改名成队列里另一组的 `worker_{hash}.lock`（哈希可从索引第一列拿到，新文件 mtime 即「现在」，锁视为有效）——再 `initialize_queue` 并反复 `get_work()` 直到返回 `None`，数一数实际领到几项、被跳过几项。

416	
417	- `initialize_queue` 返回 3（5 路径 ÷ 每组 2 = 3 组，尚无完成项）。

425	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
426	
427	**练习 1**：三级跳过检查中，哪一级不产生任何后端 IO？为什么要设计这一级？
428	
429	**答案**：第 ① 级（本地 `_completed_hash_cache` 命中）纯内存。因为队列尾部往往聚集大量已被其他机器完成的项，若每一项都去后端查 `is_completed`（S3 下是一次网络请求），开销巨大；本地缓存把绝大多数跳过变成零成本，再靠「连续 3 次命中后全量刷新」保证缓存不至于过期太久。
430	
431	**练习 2**：如果把 `mark_done` 改成「先 `delete_worker_lock` 再 `create_done_flag`」，会出什么问题？
432	
433	**答案**：在锁已删、旗未立的窗口内，另一台机器的 `get_work` 会同时通过 ②（无 done flag）和 ③（无锁）两级检查，把同一工作项重复领走、重复计算。原顺序（先旗后锁）保证放锁的那一刻完成标记已可见，把窗口堵死。
434	
435	**练习 3**：一个 worker 领了任务后进程被 kill -9，这个工作项会永远丢失吗？
436	
437	**答案**：不会。锁文件残留但其 mtime 停留在领任务时刻；30 分钟（1800 秒）后任何 worker 的 `is_worker_lock_taken` 都会判定它 stale，`get_work` 跳过检查放行、`create_worker_lock` 覆盖旧锁，该组被重新处理。结果文件是覆盖写（u2-l8），重做幂等。
438	
439	**练习 4**：`get_work` 里每跳过一个 item 都要调 `self._queue.task_done()`，这一行删掉会怎样？
440	
441	**答案**：`asyncio.Queue` 内部维护未决计数，`get_nowait()` 使计数 +1、`task_done()` 使计数 −1。跳过的项若不销账，`await queue.join()`（如果有人调用）会永远等不到归零而挂起；本仓库当前主流程未用 `join`，但销账是使用 Queue 的正确姿势，删掉属于埋雷。

443	## 5. 综合实践
444	
445	把本讲三个模块串成一个「**模拟两台机器协同处理**」的小实验。全部在本地完成，不需要 GPU 和真实 PDF（队列并不校验路径指向的文件存在与否——populate 阶段只做字符串登记，下载发生在 worker 阶段，见 u2-l2）。
446	
447	**任务**：同一 workspace，模拟「机器 A 做了一部分后崩溃 → 机器 B 接手做完」的全过程。

451	import asyncio, os, tempfile
452	from olmocr.work_queue import LocalBackend, WorkQueue
453	
454	async def machine_a(ws):
455	    """机器 A：入队 10 个路径，初始化，领 2 项做完 1 项，然后"崩溃"（不放最后一个锁）。"""
456	    wq = WorkQueue(LocalBackend(ws))
457	    await wq.populate_queue([f"/fake/docs/doc_{i}.pdf" for i in range(10)], items_per_group=2)
458	    n = await wq.initialize_queue()
459	    print(f"[A] 初始化队列: {n} 项")            # 预期 5
460	
461	    item1 = await wq.get_work()
462	    await wq.mark_done(item1)                    # 第 1 项：正常完成
463	
464	    item2 = await wq.get_work()                  # 第 2 项：领了但没做完 —— 模拟 kill -9
465	    print(f"[A] 崩溃前领走: {item2.hash[:12]}（锁未释放）")
466	
467	async def machine_b(ws):
468	    """机器 B：接手。注意 item2 的锁尚新鲜，会被跳过。"""
469	    wq = WorkQueue(LocalBackend(ws))
470	    n = await wq.initialize_queue()
471	    print(f"[B] 接手时队列: {n} 项")             # 预期 4（A 完成的 1 项被剔除）
472	
473	    done, skipped_locked = 0, 0
474	    while True:
475	        before = wq.size
476	        item = await wq.get_work()
477	        if item is None:
478	            break
479	        if wq.size == before - 1 and item.hash:  # 正常领到
480	            pass
481	        await wq.mark_done(item)
482	        done += 1
483	    # 试着统计：B 实际完成了几项？item2 是否被 B 碰过？（提示：观察 worker_locks 残留）
484	
485	async def main():
486	    ws = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="wq_two_machines_")
487	    await machine_a(ws)
488	    await machine_b(ws)
489	    print("最终 done_flags 数量:", len(os.listdir(os.path.join(ws, "done_flags"))))
490	
491	asyncio.run(main())
492	```
493	
494	**要回答的问题**：
495	
496	1. 机器 B 接手时队列为什么是 4 项而不是 3 项？（A 完成的 1 项被 done flag 剔除；A 崩溃时锁未放的 item2 **仍在队列里**，只是被锁挡住。）

498	3. 运行结束后 `worker_locks/` 里还剩几个文件？它属于谁？（剩 1 个，即 A 崩溃时留下的 item2 的锁；30 分钟后它才会被判定 stale 而可被覆盖。）
499	4. 把 `machine_a` 里领 item2 与崩溃之间的等待拉长到超过 `worker_lock_timeout_secs`（不必真等 30 分钟——可以临时给 `get_work` 传一个很小的 `worker_lock_timeout_secs=0` 试试），B 还会跳过 item2 吗？（不会，锁立即 stale，B 会覆盖锁并接手。）
500	
501	**预期结果**：最终 `done_flags` 数量为 4（A 做 1 项 + B 做 3 项，item2 被锁保护无人重做）；改为 0 超时后应为 5。以上依据源码逻辑推得，待本地验证。
502	
503	## 6. 本讲小结
504	
505	- **三层抽象**：`WorkItem`（hash + 路径组的最小任务单元）、`Backend`（索引读写/完成标记/锁共八个原语的存储接口）、`WorkQueue`（去重分组、跳过、加锁的调度语义）——换存储后端不动调度，换调度不碰存储。
506	- **populate_queue 是幂等的路径级合并**：set 去重 → 读旧索引求差集 → `sorted`（确定性切组）→ 按 `items_per_group` 切段 → 每段 `sorted` 后 sha1 得组哈希 → CSV（QUOTE_MINIMAL 转义逗号）+zstd 整文件覆盖写；已有分组一经写入即冻结。
507	- **组哈希是协调的钥匙**：排序 + utf-8 + sha1 保证跨机确定性，done flag、worker lock、结果文件名全部内容寻址到它。
508	- **initialize_queue = 重建内存视图**：从索引剔除 done 集合后 `random.shuffle` 灌入 `asyncio.Queue`——洗牌为了负载均衡与多机错峰；内存队列崩了就丢，磁盘事实（索引 + flags）才是持久状态。
509	- **get_work 的三级跳过 + mark_done 的先旗后锁**：本地缓存（零 IO）→ 逐项查 done（连续 3 次命中则全量刷新缓存）→ 查锁新鲜度（mtime 距今 ≤ 1800 秒算有主）；完成时先写 done flag 再删锁，堵死重复领取窗口。
510	- **best-effort 取向**：锁与旗操作失败一律告警继续、读操作失败一律返回「未完成/未上锁」——宁可重复计算（结果覆盖写幂等），绝不卡死流水线。
511	
512	## 7. 下一步学习建议
513	
514	本讲只点了 `LocalBackend` 的锁实现细节，并把 `S3Backend` 当黑盒。下一讲 **u3-l2《LocalBackend 与 S3Backend：同一队列的两种落地》**会逐方法对比两个后端：本地文件操作如何经 `asyncio.to_thread` + 120 秒超时进入事件循环，S3 如何用 `head_object`/`put_object`/`delete_object` 实现同一套语义，以及 `parse_s3_path`、`expand_s3_glob`、`download_zstd_csv` 等 s3_utils 函数（u4-l3 还会再深入）。建议先自己动手：把 [work_queue.py:L392-L473](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L392-L473) 的 `S3Backend` 与 LocalBackend 并排读一遍，列一张「同一方法、两种落地」的对照表，再去听下一讲核对。

# WorkQueue 抽象：Backend 接口与队列语义

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 `WorkItem`、`Backend`、`WorkQueue` 三个角色各自承担的职责，以及 Backend 接口八个方法的分工。
2. 描述 `populate_queue` 的完整流程：路径级去重 → 排序 → 按 `items_per_group` 切组 → sha1 组哈希 → CSV 编码落盘，并解释每一步为什么存在。
3. 理解 `initialize_queue` 的洗牌逻辑与 `get_work` 的三级跳过策略（本地缓存 → done 标记 → worker 锁），以及 `mark_done` 中「先立旗、后放锁」的顺序设计。
4. 亲手在一个临时 workspace 上跑通「入队 → 初始化 → 领任务 → 完成」的完整生命周期，并核对磁盘上的每一个文件。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲建立在第 1、2 单元已有认知之上，先帮你把几个关键概念补齐。

**工作队列（work queue）与任务队列。** 在 u2-l1 中我们看到，`main()` 只做编排，真正干活的是 N 个 `worker` 协程。worker 从哪里拿活？答案就是本讲的 `WorkQueue`。它是一个典型的**生产者-消费者**结构：`populate_queue` 往队列里放活，`worker` 通过 `get_work` 领活，干完后 `mark_done` 销账。

**断点续跑（resumable）。** 百万级 PDF 的批处理不可能一次跑完：机器会崩、任务会被抢占、你会主动中断。olmOCR 的做法是把队列的**持久状态**全部落在 workspace 的文件里（u1-l3 介绍过五大产物），内存里的 `asyncio.Queue` 只是每次启动时从磁盘重建出来的临时视图。本讲会精确回答「哪些东西落盘、哪些东西在内存」。

**乐观并发与「标记」语义。** 多台机器（或多个进程）可能同时指向同一个 workspace。olmOCR 不用中心化的锁服务，而是用两个约定俗成的「标记」协调：

- **done flag**：`done_flags/done_{hash}.flag`，表示某个工作项已完成，任何人都不必再做。
- **worker lock**：`worker_locks/worker_{hash}.lock`，表示某个工作项正被某个 worker 处理，别人先别碰。

这本质是一种**乐观并发控制**：先领活、后检查冲突；冲突了（锁被占）就跳过去做下一个。代价是极端情况下可能重复计算，u2-l8 讲过结果落盘是「整文件覆盖」的，所以重复计算是幂等的、可接受的。

**CSV 编码与 zstd 压缩。** 队列索引 `work_index_list.csv.zstd` 是一个 zstd 压缩的 CSV 文件，每行形如 `组哈希,路径1,路径2,...`。为什么用 CSV？因为 S3 路径、`tarball::成员名` 这类字符串完全可能包含逗号，直接用 `','.join()` 切分会切错，必须用 CSV 规则转义（加双引号）。为什么压缩？百万行的索引能省不少空间与传输量。

**sha1 与内容寻址。** sha1 把任意字节串映射成 40 个十六进制字符。olmOCR 用它给「一组路径」算出一个确定性的身份 ID——同样的路径集合无论在哪台机器上算，哈希都相同。done flag、worker lock、结果文件名（u2-l8 的 `output_{hash}.jsonl`）全部以这个哈希为键，这就是**内容寻址**（content-addressing）：ID 即内容摘要，天然去重、天然跨机一致。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 WorkItem、Backend 与 WorkQueue：一张接口地图

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`work_queue.py` 用三个类把「队列」拆成了职责清晰的三层：

- **`WorkItem`（工作项）**：最小任务单元，只有两个字段——`hash`（这组路径的身份 ID）和 `work_paths`（这组里所有待处理文档的路径）。注意队列的粒度是「一组 PDF」，不是「单个 PDF」：u2-l2 讲过 `items_per_group` 按平均页数估算，一组大约对应 `--pages_per_group`（默认 500）页，这样每个工作项的耗时大致均匀。
- **`Backend`(存储后端)**：纯接口（抽象基类），规定「队列的持久状态如何读写」。它不知道任何调度逻辑，只提供八个原语：索引的读/写、完成集合的查询、单个完成标记的查询/创建、锁的查询/创建/删除。`LocalBackend`（本地文件）与 `S3Backend`（S3 对象）是它的两个实现——同一套队列语义，两种物理落地，下一讲对比。
- **`WorkQueue`（队列本体）**：持有内存中的 `asyncio.Queue`，实现调度语义——入队去重分组、初始化剔除已完成、领任务时的跳过与加锁、完成时的销账。它通过 `Backend` 读写持久状态。

这个分层的价值：调度逻辑写一遍，换存储后端不用改一行队列代码；反之，给 Backend 加新实现（比如 GCS）也不动调度。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`WorkQueue` 的完整生命周期：

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  populate_queue(paths, items_per_group)                      │
│    去重 → 读旧索引 → 求新路径 → 排序 → 切组 → 算组哈希        │
│    → 合并旧组+新组 → Backend.save_index_lines() 落盘          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  initialize_queue()                                          │
│    读索引 → 查 done flags → 剔除已完成 → random.shuffle      │
│    → 灌入内存 asyncio.Queue → 返回队列长度                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  循环: get_work() ──► worker 处理 ──► mark_done(item)        │
│    三级跳过: 本地缓存 / done flag / worker lock               │
│    领到: create_worker_lock 后返回 WorkItem                   │
│    完成: create_done_flag + delete_worker_lock                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

对应 pipeline.py 中的真实调用点：`main()` 创建队列（本地或 S3）、`--pdfs` 存在时填充、推理前初始化，然后交给 worker 循环消费。

### 4.2 populate_queue：去重、分组与 sha1 组哈希

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`populate_queue(work_paths, items_per_group)` 解决的问题是：**把一批新文档路径幂等地并入队列索引**。三个关键词：

- **幂等**：同一批路径重复传入不会产生重复分组。pipeline 里 `main()` 每次带 `--pdfs` 启动都会调用它，重跑是常态。
- **分组**：新路径按 `items_per_group` 个一组切分。u2-l2 讲过这个数由「目标页数 ÷ 平均页数」估出；tarball 则固定每组 1 个（见 pipeline.py 的两次调用）。
- **组哈希**：每组算一个 sha1 作为身份。这个哈希是后续一切协调的钥匙——done flag、worker lock、结果文件名都用它。

为什么哈希前要先 `sorted`？因为 Python 的 set 迭代顺序受字符串哈希随机化影响（PYTHONHASHSEED），同一组路径在不同进程里的顺序可能不同。先排序再哈希，保证**任何机器、任何时刻**对同一路径集合算出同一个 ID。公式化地说，对路径集合 \( G \)：

\[ \mathrm{hash}(G) = \mathrm{sha1}\big(\,\texttt{utf8}(p_1) \,\Vert\, \texttt{utf8}(p_2) \,\Vert\, \cdots \,\Vert\, \texttt{utf8}(p_k)\,\big), \quad p_1 < p_2 < \cdots < p_k = \mathrm{sorted}(G) \]

其中 \( \Vert \) 表示字节串直接拼接（无分隔符）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`populate_queue` 的执行步骤（伪代码）：

```text
输入: work_paths（新一批路径）, items_per_group
1. all_paths  = set(work_paths)                # 入参级去重
2. lines      = backend.load_index_lines()      # 读现有索引
3. existing   = 解析 lines → {组哈希: [路径...]}
4. existing_paths = existing 中所有路径摊平成集合
5. new_paths  = sorted(all_paths - existing_paths)   # 跨批次去重 + 排序
6. 若 new_paths 为空 → 直接返回（什么都不写）
7. 把 new_paths 按 items_per_group 逐段切片
   每段算 _compute_workgroup_hash(段) → 得到 (组哈希, 段)
8. combined = existing ∪ 新组                  # 同哈希时新组覆盖旧组
9. backend.save_index_lines(编码后的 combined)  # 整文件覆盖写
```

两个值得咀嚼的细节：

- **去重是路径级的，不是组级的**。第 5 步在「路径」粒度上做差集。后果：如果第二次运行换了 `items_per_group`，**已有分组不会被重新切分**——旧路径全部命中 `existing_paths` 被剔除，只有新增路径按新的组大小分组。索引一旦写入，分组就冻结了。
- **第 5 步的 `sorted` 有双重作用**：既让分组结果确定（同批路径在任何机器上切出相同的组），也让组内顺序确定，进一步稳定组哈希。

CSV 编解码是索引的「物理格式」层：每行 `[组哈希, 路径1, 路径2, ...]` 用 `csv.writer` 的 `QUOTE_MINIMAL` 规则转义——只有含逗号/引号的字段才会被双引号包裹，其余裸写。

### 4.3 initialize_queue 与 get_work：洗牌、三级跳过与锁

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

消费侧要回答三个问题：

**一、启动时队列从哪来？** `initialize_queue` 把索引重建为内存队列：剔除已有 done flag 的组，剩余的 `random.shuffle` 打乱后灌进 `asyncio.Queue`。为什么要洗牌？两个理由：(1) **负载均衡**——索引按路径排序切组，相邻路径往往同源同长短，不洗牌的话耗时大户可能聚堆，多个 worker 快慢悬殊；(2) **多机错峰**——若两台机器都从头按序消费，会在同样的项目上反复撞锁；随机起点让它们自然散开。

**二、领任务时要检查什么？** 内存队列是启动时刻的快照，别的 worker/机器此后可能已经完成了其中某些项。所以 `get_work` 每弹出一项要做**三级跳过检查**：

1. 本地 `_completed_hash_cache` 命中 → 跳过（纯内存，零后端 IO）；
2. 后端 `is_completed(hash)` → 跳过（一次后端查询）；
3. 后端 `is_worker_lock_taken(hash)` 锁被占且未过期 → 跳过（别人正在做）。

三级全过 → `create_worker_lock` 抢锁，把这项返回给 worker。

**三、锁为什么会「过期」？** worker 崩溃时不会有人来放锁，锁文件会永久残留。olmOCR 的解法是**锁自带新鲜度**：锁是否有效看它的 mtime 距今是否超过 `worker_lock_timeout_secs`（默认 1800 秒）：

\[ \text{锁有效} \iff now - \mathrm{mtime}(\text{lock}) \leq 1800\,\text{s} \]

超过 30 分钟的锁视为 stale（主人大概率已死），`create_worker_lock` 直接覆盖它（见 [L210](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L210) 的注释 "Create lock (overwrites if stale)"）。这要求工作项的处理时长明显小于 30 分钟——分组大小（约 500 页）正是按这个量级校准的。

**best-effort 语义**：锁与旗的写操作失败时只 `logger.warning` 然后继续，不抛异常（LocalBackend 中尤为明确，见 [L339-L351](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L339-L351) 的注释 "duplicate work is okay"）。因为最坏结果只是重复计算，而结果落盘是覆盖写、幂等（u2-l8）；反之，为了严格锁语义而让流水线卡死才是不可接受的。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`initialize_queue`：

```text
1. lines = backend.load_index_lines()
2. work_queue = 解析 lines → {组哈希: [路径...]}
3. done_hashes = backend.get_completed_hashes()      # 全量已完成集合
4. remaining = work_queue 的键 - done_hashes
5. remaining_items = [WorkItem(hash=h, work_paths=...) for h in remaining]
6. random.shuffle(remaining_items)                    # 洗牌
7. 重建空 self._queue，逐项 put 进去
8. 返回 self.size
```

`get_work` 的主循环：

```text
while True:
    item = self._queue.get_nowait()          # 队列空 → 返回 None（worker 退出）
    ① item.hash ∈ 本地已完成缓存 → task_done, continue
    ② backend.is_completed(item.hash)  为真 → task_done, continue
       连续 ② 命中满 3 次 → 全量刷新本地缓存（此后走①）
    ③ backend.is_worker_lock_taken(item.hash) 为真 → task_done, continue
    ④ backend.create_worker_lock(item.hash)  # 失败仅告警并 continue
    重置连续命中计数，返回 item
```

`mark_done`：

```text
1. backend.create_done_flag(item.hash)     # 先立旗
2. backend.delete_worker_lock(item.hash)   # 后放锁
3. self._queue.task_done()                 # 销账
```

顺序很关键：**先立旗再放锁**。若反过来（先放锁后立旗），存在一个窗口——锁已删、旗未写——另一个 worker 恰好在此窗口检查会同时通过 ②③，把同一项重复领走。旗先落地，放锁瞬间该 item 已在完成集合里，任何并发检查都会被 ② 拦下。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：三级跳过检查中，哪一级不产生任何后端 IO？为什么要设计这一级？

**答案**：第 ① 级（本地 `_completed_hash_cache` 命中）纯内存。因为队列尾部往往聚集大量已被其他机器完成的项，若每一项都去后端查 `is_completed`（S3 下是一次网络请求），开销巨大；本地缓存把绝大多数跳过变成零成本，再靠「连续 3 次命中后全量刷新」保证缓存不至于过期太久。

**练习 2**：如果把 `mark_done` 改成「先 `delete_worker_lock` 再 `create_done_flag`」，会出什么问题？

**答案**：在锁已删、旗未立的窗口内，另一台机器的 `get_work` 会同时通过 ②（无 done flag）和 ③（无锁）两级检查，把同一工作项重复领走、重复计算。原顺序（先旗后锁）保证放锁的那一刻完成标记已可见，把窗口堵死。

**练习 3**：一个 worker 领了任务后进程被 kill -9，这个工作项会永远丢失吗？

**答案**：不会。锁文件残留但其 mtime 停留在领任务时刻；30 分钟（1800 秒）后任何 worker 的 `is_worker_lock_taken` 都会判定它 stale，`get_work` 跳过检查放行、`create_worker_lock` 覆盖旧锁，该组被重新处理。结果文件是覆盖写（u2-l8），重做幂等。

**练习 4**：`get_work` 里每跳过一个 item 都要调 `self._queue.task_done()`，这一行删掉会怎样？

**答案**：`asyncio.Queue` 内部维护未决计数，`get_nowait()` 使计数 +1、`task_done()` 使计数 −1。跳过的项若不销账，`await queue.join()`（如果有人调用）会永远等不到归零而挂起；本仓库当前主流程未用 `join`，但销账是使用 Queue 的正确姿势，删掉属于埋雷。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
